prospect.name: Everett
prospect.location: United States, Eastern Standard Time zone
prospect.occupation: Works in a nursing home on roughly 7am-to-7pm shifts, including some night shifts; actively seeking a new, higher-paying job
prospect.family_status: Came out of a relationship a couple of months before the call; has a son who gave him a jumper he cannot yet fit into
prospect.training_background: Effectively untrained until a few months ago. Never trained as a teenager or adult — 'barely touched any exercise equipment, even growing up'. Started going to a gym after a breakup, using machines without any structure or plan. Struggled with a barbell and is 'nowhere close' to deadlifting bodyweight. Has had business and leadership coaching but never a fitness coach. No kettlebell experience and does not yet own one.
prospect.medical: Self-disclosed diabetes, managed with multiple daily medications — 'I know I'm 43, I have diabetes' and 'I do take a lot of pills, and I do not like that'. Recurrent shoulder pain that flares under pressing movements — 'if I shoulder press, that's like something that does actually flare up'. Neither the diabetes, the medications nor the shoulder was explored by the rep, and no physician, specialist or clearance was mentioned at any point in the call.

signals: Proposed label: the_turnaround_starter — a first-time trainee with an active chronic condition and acute financial distress, triggered into action by a life rupture rather than by ambition. He is not recovering a former self because there is no former self: he was never fit, never trained, and describes himself as an unhealthy kid and teenager. That rules out the_rebuilder, which is otherwise the nearest listed archetype.
The trigger is explicitly a breakup: 'I want to come out on top out of this break. I want to be in the best shape of my life. I want to get a new job.'
Motivation is very high and resistance to the offer was zero on value — 'I would jump on it if I had the money' — with the entire blocker being capacity to pay
Not the_prehab_fighter: the diabetes is long-standing and chronic rather than a new acute diagnosis being fought, and he does not frame training as part of a treatment battle

goals.text: Get shredded and visibly defined — 'get into the best shape of my life'
Increase strength, having struggled with a bare barbell and being nowhere near deadlifting bodyweight
Improve mobility and reduce general stiffness, particularly hips
Stay mobile and independent into old age — explicitly, to avoid ending up in a nursing home like the residents he cares for
Fit into a jumper his son gave him three to five years ago, and drop a couple of clothing sizes
Build confidence after a breakup and carry himself differently
Gain energy and presence to support getting a new, better-paying job
Improve overall health given his diabetes and reduce reliance on medication
Learn the reasoning behind training and nutrition so he can sustain it without a coach

pains.text: Has diabetes and takes multiple daily medications, which he dislikes and links to his weight
Shoulder pain that flares badly under pressing movements — 'it's just like hurt, like hell'
Trains with no structure at all — 'whatever I see, like wherever I feel'
Has wanted to address his fitness for years without acting on it — 'a goal I've been procrastinating on'
Orders takeaway three to four days a week alongside canteen food at work
Severe financial distress: checking account overdrawn by $76, no money until payday, credit score around 545, single debit card and no usable credit
Emotional fallout from a recent breakup, which is the stated trigger for acting now
Works 7am-to-7pm and night shifts, making meal timing and routine hard to structure
Struggles to picture a better future for himself — repeatedly could not answer visualisation questions and said 'I'm really trying not to overthink this'
No experience of what good training looks like, having never worked with a fitness coach

objections.raw_quote: 6K. Is this something I can break down into payments?
objections.rep_response: Isolated the objection correctly first — 'outside of the investment, do you feel like, yeah, Richard, let's just do this?' — then ran the financial picture (checking balance, credit score, number of cards) and offered an internal instalment plan of 'six times 1,200'.

objections.raw_quote: Today? would say no, because my account is actually negative $76 because of like builds and other things.
objections.rep_response: Having already been told nothing was available until Friday, the rep asked for a $100 deposit that same day. On learning the account was overdrawn he probed whether there were other cards — 'Is that negative just the only card that you have, or do you have multiple cards that you usually use?' — then said he would not want to put the prospect in a difficult financial position, and settled on the prospect texting him on Thursday to make the deposit.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep stated third-party financing was unavailable because it requires roughly a 600 credit score and the prospect self-reported around 545. He then offered an internal plan: 'What we can do internally is maximum six times. Maximum six would come down to, yeah, so six times 1,200.' That totals $7,200 against a $6,000 offer. When the prospect restated it as 'what, 1,000 a month or whatever', the rep replied 'Yeah, so like a little bit more than 1,000 a month' and the $1,200 gap was never identified or explained. Separately a $100 deposit was requested to hold a slot, and the rep said coaching could only begin once the first term of 'like 1,200 or so' was paid.

evidence: No money changed hands and no payment link was sent — the rep sent only his personal phone number: 'I will send you my personal number so you can actually reach out to me.'
Prospect was unambiguously willing but unable: 'Oh, definitely. I would jump on it if I had the money.'
Prospect stated he had nothing available: 'Right now, to be honest with I will not have any money until Friday. So nothing is available.' and 'my account is actually negative $76'.
Agreed next step was for the prospect to text the rep on Thursday to make a $100 deposit, with a first instalment the following week.
The onboarding call with Trevor was explicitly withheld pending payment: 'Trevor doesn't book like onboarding meetings until we have got one month in.'

Counter-evidence: strong verbal commitment throughout ('Oh, definitely, yes. Yes.' and 'I definitely want it. I'm not going to sit there and say like no.'), so intent is high even though nothing was collected.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to text the rep around 10am Thursday to pay a $100 deposit; a further call the week after to take the first instalment and book onboarding with Trevor.

notable.note: The most serious call in this batch on two independent axes. Clinically, the prospect disclosed diabetes managed with multiple daily medications and a shoulder that flares under pressing, and was then walked through a programme of progressively loaded kettlebell work with no clinician clearance sought and no follow-up on either disclosure. Commercially, the rep quoted an internal plan of six payments of $1,200 — $7,200 against a $6,000 offer — and let the prospect's own restatement of roughly $1,000 a month stand uncorrected. He also asked for a same-day $100 deposit from a man who had just said his account was overdrawn by $76, and probed for additional cards, though he did later say he would not want to put him in a difficult position. The prospect sits outside every stated ICP criterion.

quality.notes: Frequent speaker inversion, including whole passages. The height and age exchange around 00:01:38 is inverted so that '43' and 'About 6'2"' appear under the wrong labels, and long stretches from 00:10:30 to 00:11:30 and 00:16:00 to 00:16:30 swap rep questions onto the prospect. Roles resolved from content throughout. One factual contradiction the transcript does not resolve: the prospect first gives his weight as 'about 238 or something like so' and later says 'I'm literally 260' while discussing his diabetes; 238 is recorded because it was the answer to the direct question and the rep recapped it back as 238 without correction.
